$comment: The concept map of the Īśāvāsya. Hand-authored: nodes are groups of mantras, edges are relations. kind 'textual' = stated or implied by the text's own sequence; 'interpretive' = a reading of a commentator or the editor (the note says whose). Coordinates are in the SVG viewBox.
intro: The eighteen mantras as a web of teachings. Solid lines follow the text’s own sequence and wording; dashed lines are interpretive links, each attributed.
desc: Fifteen teachings of the Īśāvāsya Upaniṣad, from the Lord dwelling in all things to the final prayer to Agni, with the relations between them.

nodes.label: The Lord in all this
nodes.text: All this, whatever moves in the moving world, is to be covered or dwelt in by the Lord. The opening vision, from which the rest unfolds.

nodes.label: Let go, and enjoy
nodes.text: With that given up, enjoy; do not covet — whose is wealth? The first instruction, read differently by each commentator.

nodes.label: Act without clinging
nodes.text: Doing works here, one may wish to live a hundred years; action does not cling to such a person.

nodes.label: Worlds of blind darkness
nodes.text: Those who slay the self go after death to worlds covered in blind darkness.

nodes.label: Unmoving, swifter than mind
nodes.text: The one that does not move is faster than the mind; it moves and does not move; it is far and near, within all this and outside it.

nodes.label: All beings in the self
nodes.text: One who sees all beings in the self, and the self in all beings, does not shrink from anything.

nodes.label: No delusion, no grief
nodes.text: For the knower in whom all beings have become the self, what delusion, what grief, seeing oneness?

nodes.label: The bright, bodiless one
nodes.text: He has gone round — bright, bodiless, without wound or sinew, pure, untouched by evil; the seer, wise, all-encompassing, self-existent, who ordered things for endless years.

nodes.label: Vidyā and avidyā
nodes.text: Both alone lead into darkness; each has its own result; knowing both together, one crosses death and attains immortality.

nodes.label: Sambhūti and asambhūti
nodes.text: The same pattern again with becoming and non-becoming: each alone leads to darkness, both together cross death.

nodes.label: The golden lid
nodes.text: The face of the real is covered by a golden vessel; uncover it, Pūṣan, for one whose dharma is truth, to see.

nodes.label: That person I am
nodes.text: Draw back your rays; I see your fairest form. That person yonder — I am he.

nodes.label: Breath to air, body to ash
nodes.text: Breath to the immortal air, this body ending in ash. Om, mind, remember what was done.

nodes.label: Lead by a good path
nodes.text: Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth; you know all ways; keep crooked fault from us; we offer you our fullest homage.

edges.label: or else
edges.note: Śaṅkara: mantra 1 is for the renouncer, mantra 2 for the one who cannot renounce.

edges.label: contrast
edges.note: Mantra 3 follows as the fate of those who obscure the self.

edges.label: described as
edges.note: The commentators read 4–5 as describing the reality named in mantra 1.

edges.label: and as
edges.note: Mantra 8 describes the same ‘he’ positively and by negation.

edges.label: known as
edges.note: The knower of 6–7 sees what 4–5 and 8 describe.

edges.label: works and knowledge
edges.note: Śaṅkara and Deśika both read avidyā in 9–11 as action (karma).

edges.label: same pattern
edges.note: Mantras 12–14 repeat the form of 9–11 word for word apart from the paired terms.

edges.label: echo
edges.note: Editor’s note: ‘so ’ham asmi’ (16) recalls the self seen in all (6–7); the commentators differ on what the identification means.

edges.label: uncovered
edges.note: The lid removed (15), the form is seen (16).

edges.label: then
edges.note: The dying person’s prayers in sequence; BU 5.15.1 has the same order.

edges.label: the way of the gods
edges.note: Śaṅkara: the one who has combined works and meditation asks at death for the path of light.
